h1: Do I need a building permit to replace a roof in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Roof Replacement Permits: Re-Shingling and Structural Work
description: Understand the difference between ordinary roof repairs and work that changes structural supports, and check historic review before replacing roof materials.
short_answer: The Massachusetts building code exempts ordinary repairs from a building permit, but work involving substantial removal or alteration of structural supports is not treated as an ordinary repair. Newton has a specific roofing and siding permit application category, so homeowners should confirm the current application requirement for their exact roof scope.

facts.text: The state building code says an application or notice is not required for ordinary repairs, but separately identifies substantial cutting of structural members and removal or alteration of load-bearing supports as work requiring a permit.
Newton ISD has separated permit applications into specific work categories, including roofing and siding.

qa.q: Does every roof replacement require a building permit in Newton?
qa.a: The sources reviewed do not establish a universal rule for every roof replacement method. Confirm whether the proposed stripping, overlay, decking, or structural work requires a Newton building permit.

items: Whether the project is ordinary repair, full replacement, or structural alteration
Whether roof decking, rafters, trusses, or other structural members will be changed
Whether an overlay is allowed for the existing roof condition
The current Newton roofing application and inspection requirements
Whether the property is in a Local Historic District or is a Landmark
